subject: c10-hin

weightage.label: Textbooks: Kshitij Prose 11, Kshitij Poetry 11, Kritika 8 (Ch 3 to 5)

note: Marks are official (theory total 80, internal assessment 20 = 5 each for periodic, multiple assessment, portfolio, and listening and speaking). Section A: unseen passage 7 (about 250 words) and unseen poem 7 (about 120 words). Section B: grammar 16 (sentence types, voice, parts of speech, figures of speech: attempt 4 of 5 in each). Section D: paragraph 6, letter 5, resume or e-mail 5, advertisement or message 4. No questions will be asked from these lessons. Kshitij Poetry: Dev (Savaiya, Kavitt), Chhaya Mat Chhoona, Kanyadaan. Kshitij Prose: Stri-Shiksha ke Virodhi Kutarkon ka Khandan, Manaviya Karuna ki Divya Chamak. Kritika: Ehi Thaiyan Jhulni Herani Ho Rama, George Pancham ki Naak.
mistakes: Do not spend board-exam study time on the lessons listed as excluded in the note above.
Grammar: in each of the four topics you answer 4 out of 5 questions. Read all five and pick the ones you are surest of.
Writing tasks have word limits: paragraph about 120 words, letter about 100, resume or e-mail about 80, advertisement or message about 40. Keep to them.
Unseen passage and poem: answer from the passage itself.
Kritika answers have a limit of 50 to 60 words, and Kshitij short answers 25 to 30 words. Keep them to the point.
Learn the five figures of speech in the syllabus: upama, roopak, utpreksha, atishyokti and maanveekaran.
order: Textbooks first (Ch 3 to 5, 30 marks): read each lesson and poem that is included, and write short notes.
Then creative writing (20 marks): practise the paragraph, letter, resume or e-mail, and advertisement or message in turn.
Then grammar (16 marks) and unseen passages (14 marks): practise a little each week.
Keep periodic assessment, portfolio and listening and speaking (20 internal marks) on schedule with your school.
